TB-500 in Canada: Synthetic Thymosin β4, Tested by Batch

What is actually in a TB-500 vial, why the naming confusion matters commercially, and how to verify a lot

July 30, 2026·By Adam Reeves · Research Editor, Eppix Labs

TB-500 has a naming problem that is worth resolving before anything else, because it changes what you are comparing when you compare prices. The research literature is about thymosin β4, a 43-residue protein. On the research market the name "TB-500" is used both for synthetic full-length thymosin β4 and for short fragments of it, most often the seven-residue Ac-LKKTETQ. They are not the same molecule, and a vial priced against one is not comparable to a vial containing the other.

The Eppix Labs TB-500 is synthetic full-length thymosin β4. This article covers what the thymosin β4 literature supports, what a TB-500 certificate should tell you, and the regulatory position in Canada as of August 2026. TB-500 is supplied for in-vitro laboratory research only.

What TB-500 is, and what it is not

Thymosin β4 is a 43-amino-acid, 4.9 kDa actin-sequestering protein present in most mammalian cells, first characterized as a thymic peptide and later shown to be a major intracellular G-actin binding protein.[1] Its actin-binding activity localizes substantially to the heptapeptide motif LKKTETQ, residues 17 to 23.

That motif, acetylated, is also sold as "TB-500". It is under a fifth of the mass of the parent protein (889 g/mol against roughly 4,963 g/mol), which is exactly why the name alone tells you nothing. The measured mass on a certificate is unambiguous: an identity result near 4.96 kDa is the full protein, one near 0.89 kDa is the fragment.

Sequence and structure

Forty-three residues, N-terminally acetylated in the native form, with the actin-binding LKKTETQ motif in the first half of the chain. A sequence this long is a harder synthesis than a short fragment, which is why substitution with a cheaper short peptide is the most economically attractive form of adulteration for this product, and why an MS identity line on the certificate is worth insisting on: a purity assay alone cannot see it.

What the published research shows

The substantive literature is on thymosin β4 itself, the molecule this product is, rather than on any short fragment:

  • ·Actin sequestration. Thymosin β4 is the principal G-actin sequestering protein in mammalian cells, and the actin-binding function is the mechanistic anchor for everything downstream.[1]
  • ·Dermal wound models. Malinda et al. (1999) reported accelerated wound healing and increased keratinocyte migration in full-thickness rat and mouse models.[2]
  • ·Corneal models. Sosne et al. (2002) reported promotion of corneal epithelial wound healing and reduction of inflammation in an experimental model.[3]
  • ·Cardiac models. Bock-Marquette et al. (2004) reported activation of integrin-linked kinase and improved cardiac cell migration and survival after coronary artery ligation in mice.[4]
  • ·Breadth of animal work. Philp and Kleinman (2010) survey the animal literature across dermal, corneal and cardiac repair models.[5]

The limit of the evidence

Thymosin β4 reached human clinical investigation in dermal and corneal indications and has no approved indication. There is no established human dose and no jurisdiction in which it is authorized for human use.

Reading full-length thymosin β4 data as if it applied to a seven-residue fragment is the single most common error in TB-500 marketing copy. The fragment carries the actin-binding motif; whether it reproduces the parent protein's behaviour in any given model is a question the published work has largely not asked.

Regulatory status: the July 2026 advisory vote

On 23 and 24 July 2026 the US FDA's Pharmacy Compounding Advisory Committee reviewed TB-500 for inclusion on the Section 503A Bulk Drug Substances List, alongside BPC-157, KPV, TB-500, MOTS-c, Epitalon and Semax. FDA staff had recommended against inclusion for every substance under review, citing insufficient characterization, little or no human effectiveness evidence, and inadequate human safety data. The committee voted in favour anyway. The vote was 8 in favour, 6 against, 1 abstention.

What the vote does not do:

  • ·It is non-binding. The committee advises, it does not decide. No final FDA determination has been issued and none of the six peptides appears in 21 CFR 216.23.
  • ·It does not make the compound an FDA-approved drug, and it establishes nothing about efficacy.
  • ·It has no effect in Canada. Health Canada has issued no authorization for human or veterinary use, and the compound remains a laboratory research material here.
  • ·It does not legitimize research-chemical retail. A compounding-list decision concerns licensed pharmacists preparing patient-specific prescriptions, which is a different channel entirely.

Verifying a TB-500 lot

Three numbers, and they are not interchangeable. Identity by mass spectrometry establishes that the material is full-length thymosin β4 and not a short fragment or a cheaper substitute. Purity by HPLC establishes what fraction of the vial contents is that compound. Measured content establishes how much is in the vial against the labelled amount. Underfilling is the failure mode that a purity-only certificate cannot detect, and it is the one a buyer pays for directly.

Frequently Asked

Is TB-500 the same thing as thymosin beta-4?

It depends on the supplier. The Eppix Labs TB-500 is synthetic full-length thymosin β4, the 43-residue, 4.9 kDa protein most published research is about. Some vials sold as "TB-500" instead contain the acetylated seven-residue fragment Ac-LKKTETQ, under a fifth of the mass. The MS identity result on the certificate tells you which.

Is TB-500 legal in Canada?

It may be sold and held as a laboratory research material. It is not authorized by Health Canada for human or veterinary use. This is not legal advice.

Did the FDA approve TB-500 in 2026?

No. An FDA advisory committee voted 8-6 in July 2026 to recommend it for the Section 503A compounding bulks list, against FDA staff's own recommendation. The vote is non-binding, no final determination has been issued, and it has no effect in Canada.

What should a TB-500 certificate show?

Batch number matching the vial, the named testing laboratory with an independent verification path, MS identity confirmation against the thymosin β4 mass near 4,963 Da, HPLC purity, and measured vial content against the labelled amount.

Is TB-500 banned in sport?

TB-500 and thymosin β4 appear on the World Anti-Doping Agency Prohibited List under growth factors affecting muscle, tendon or ligament. That is a competition matter and is separate from its status as a research material; it is noted here because researchers working with athletes ask.

How is TB-500 stored?

Lyophilized: cool, dry, dark, at -20 °C for long-term storage. Reconstituted: refrigerated, used within the window your protocol defines. See the peptide storage guide.
